applicant_utility.summary: Cranfield's GMAT-style gating is operational: you cannot even open the scholarship form until your admissions application has produced a six digit student ID, so apply for the course months before May, not weeks. The four written answers are the entire competition - each capped at 1000 characters - and they ask precisely for motivation, career significance, leadership evidence and advocacy for the campaign, so draft them offline and paste in. Only one student from Bangladesh wins, and the award replaces any other Cranfield scholarship, so this is an all-or-nothing swap rather than a stackable top-up.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Bangladeshi passport holders resident in Bangladesh with a place on an eligible Cranfield full-time MSc starting September or October, who can write crisply about leadership and career purpose.
application_readiness_checklist: Apply for admission early enough to hold a six digit Cranfield student ID well before the deadline
Check your course is on the published eligible-courses list and starts in September or October of the award year
Draft the four answers offline against the 250-1000 character limits before opening the form
Decide in advance whether you would accept this £10,000 in place of any other Cranfield scholarship, since it replaces them
common_rejection_risks: Applying for the scholarship without a six digit student ID, which blocks submission
Overshooting the 1000-character limit or underfilling the 250-character minimum on any of the four answers
Choosing a course that is not on the eligible list or that starts outside September or October
Generic leadership language with no concrete examples - evidence of leadership experience is an explicit criterion
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The £10,000 covers only part of tuition; Cranfield MSc fees typically exceed this, and living costs, flights and visa expenses are not funded.
document_audit: You need the six digit student ID from admissions before the form will accept you - it is effectively a required document
There is no separate CV or transcript upload for this scholarship; the four written answers carry the whole assessment
alerts: If awarded, this scholarship replaces any other scholarship awarded by Cranfield University - it cannot be combined
Cranfield does not routinely provide feedback on unsuccessful applications; you must email the Admissions Office to request any
Competition includes course-capacity dynamics - the page notes applications can be unsuccessful where demand exceeds places on a course
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Course application first, then the online scholarship form via the Apply Now link once the student ID exists; four written answers submitted before the deadline; all applicants notified by end of June.

applicant_utility.summary: Country fit is everything here: Edinburgh's 2026 GREAT Scholarships are restricted to nationals and residents of Thailand, Mexico and Ghana, and each country has its own published list of eligible one-year on-campus MSc programmes - verify your programme is on your country's list before applying. There are only three awards in total across the three countries, so this is a small, competitive pot. The published page presents the 2026 round without a visible application deadline in the content reviewed, so the practical move is to watch Edinburgh's funding pages and the British Council Study UK site for the next cycle's instructions rather than relying on third-party listings.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Nationals and residents of Thailand, Mexico or Ghana admitted full-time to an eligible one-year on-campus Edinburgh Master's who can evidence strong academic merit.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your programme appears on the eligible-programmes list for your country (separate PDFs exist for Mexico, Thailand and Ghana)
Check that your course is one-year, on-campus and full-time - longer or online programmes fall outside the scheme
Be ready to consent in writing to British Council contact for pre-departure briefings, reporting, evaluation and promotion
Monitor Edinburgh's scholarships pages and Study UK for the next cycle's application instructions and deadline
common_rejection_risks: Applying from a country outside Thailand, Mexico or Ghana - note that the wider GREAT campaign covers many countries but Edinburgh's own awards do not
Enrolling on a programme missing from your country's eligible-programmes list
Applying for a part-time, online or multi-year programme, which the scheme excludes
Assuming the award covers living costs or travel - it is a minimum £10,000 tuition contribution
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award provides a minimum of £10,000 toward study costs; Edinburgh living costs, flights and visa expenses are not covered by the scholarship.
document_audit: Admission to the eligible programme is the core requirement - scholarship consideration follows the admissions decision
